items.author: Ben (2026-09-08, describing round 4 against the live app); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: The levers that keep round 4 multipolar - culture, logistics, communication, succession
items.design:
RETURNED TO THE POOL 2026-09-09, unbuilt and unchanged. This was planned for sprint 36 and never started. Ben redirected that sprint mid-flight: the rules for initial colonisation and the peaceful spreading of societies are vastly different from those of war and empire, and this item is EMPIRE-PHASE - it only bites once there is something to fight over. Applying it to a span that is overwhelmingly settlement (839 foundings against 9 battles on seed 0, measured) is what would force the fixture-fitting the redirect exists to avoid. Re-scope it against whatever phase boundary sprint 37 settles on before building it.

BEN ASKED FOR LEVERS THAT STOP A TOTAL HEGEMON and named two - cultures in region, and a simple logistics implementation - leaving the rest to judgement. They serve BL-224's non-hegemony invariant, and the constraint on every one of them is the standing rule: a lever is a FORCE WITH A VISIBLE CAUSE ON THE MAP, never a term inside an actor and never a penalty that scales with a polity's rank.

THE SIX, with what exists today. (1) CULTURES IN A REGION - foreign-culture ground costs cohesion to hold and assimilates slowly, so conquest buys unrest rather than strength. PARTLY BUILT: w_cult = 150 and a per-region culture index are already in history_sim.hpp, so this is calibration more than construction. (2) SIMPLE LOGISTICS - reach falls with distance from the seat along real terrain, so a campaign past reach cannot be sustained. This is the lever that makes a strait or a mountain stall a frontier WITHOUT special-casing either, which is why it is worth more than its cost. OWED. (3) COMMUNICATION - a polity cannot act on ground it cannot hear from until a communication rung is reached. OWED, and it is also the second rung of Ben's own arc, so it earns its place twice. (4) SUCCESSION - a large polity fractures on a leadership transition, weighted by cohesion; this is the dark-age rung. COLLAPSE.md already owns culmination. (5) STRAIN - already built, and its accumulators already cross the pass 1 -> pass 2 handoff. (6) BALANCING COALITIONS - neighbours' stance moves against the largest polity.

LEVER 6 IS THE DANGEROUS ONE and is called out rather than dropped. It is one step from an agent handicap: a coefficient that reads a polity's rank and pushes back is exactly the shape the standing rule forbids. It is admissible ONLY as a STANCE the player can read on the map (RELATIONS.md), arrived at by an in-world cause. If it cannot be built that way, it is not built.

DONE WHEN: across a SEED SWEEP - not one seed - a single polity holding the great majority of the world's land at 1200 CE is rare rather than typical, and each shipped lever demonstrably moves that distribution when varied. A world that does produce a near-hegemon stays a legitimate outcome; the levers tune the forces, they do not clamp the result.

BEN'S ENDING SPEC, 2026-09-09 (elicitation notes): 'this phase will feed directly into our industrial era sim, where we see resources as capital, so it's important to keep in mind specifically how larger empires may persist, expand their reach, and then collapse into smaller nations ready for an industrial boom.'

THAT MAKES NON-HEGEMONY AN INPUT REQUIREMENT, not just a watchability one. Pass 2 is an economy pass over NATIONS, and nations are what an empire leaves behind when it can no longer hold itself. So a world ending pass 1 as one hegemon has failed the handoff however plausible its numbers -- and so has a world that never assembled anything larger than a city state. Both ends produce an industrial era with nothing to industrialise against.

REACH-GATING IS NOW THE PRIMARY LEVER, and it changes this item's shape. BL-837 was settled on 2026-09-09 as a GATE rather than a price, so lever (2) is no longer 'simple logistics' among six -- an empire persists while its network holds and fragments when it does not, and the number of nations at 1200 CE is a consequence of what got built and stayed maintainable. Re-read the other five as SUPPORTING that mechanism rather than substituting for it, and drop any that only duplicate it.

NEVER A TARGET COUNT AND NEVER A COLLAPSE EVENT FIRED AT A DATE.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-08, on the holistic scorer: diplomacy, logistics, turbulence); Claude
items.title: Neighbours coalesce against a riser out of fear of being next - the scorer second question
items.design:
RETURNED TO THE POOL 2026-09-09, unbuilt and unchanged. This was planned for sprint 36 and never started. Ben redirected that sprint mid-flight: the rules for initial colonisation and the peaceful spreading of societies are vastly different from those of war and empire, and this item is EMPIRE-PHASE - it only bites once there is something to fight over. Applying it to a span that is overwhelmingly settlement (839 foundings against 9 battles on seed 0, measured) is what would force the fixture-fitting the redirect exists to avoid. Re-scope it against whatever phase boundary sprint 37 settles on before building it.

BEN, 2026-09-08, giving the balancing-coalition lever the cause it was missing: the scorer must ask "will others attack me for fear of being wiped out next?"

THIS IS WHAT MAKES THE LEVER ADMISSIBLE, and the distinction is the whole point rather than a technicality. GENERATION_STRATEGY.md marked balancing coalitions the DANGEROUS lever, because a term that reads a polity's RANK and pushes back is an agent handicap in a diplomacy costume - precisely the shape the standing rule against agent handicaps forbids. Fear of annihilation reads a BEHAVIOUR instead: what this polity has actually done, to whom, on ground a player can point at.

THE RECORD IT READS ALREADY EXISTS. BL-827's grudge ledger is directed, decaying, and carries named events with a place and a date. A coalition forming against a riser is therefore explicable on the map - the player can ask WHY and get a list of what that polity did - which is the bar every in-world force in this project has to clear.

IT MUST NOT BECOME A RANK TERM BY THE BACK DOOR. 'Largest polity' is not the trigger; 'the polity that has been doing this to people like me' is. A quiet reimplementation as a size coefficient would pass every test here and violate the rule the item exists to satisfy - so the check must be that a large but peaceful polity attracts NO coalition, while a smaller aggressive one does.

AND IT IS BASIC, DELIBERATELY. This is a fear response inside the Era -1 sim, not a diplomacy layer: no treaties, no negotiation, no alliance objects. Two of BL-827's four grudge kinds ('a union refused', 'an ally abandoned') remain unbuilt for exactly that reason and stay unbuilt here.

DONE WHEN: a large peaceful polity attracts no coalition and a smaller aggressive one does; the coalition's cause is printable as the events behind it; and hegemony frequency falls across a seed sweep without any term reading size.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-08, on the holistic scorer: diplomacy, logistics, turbulence); Claude
items.title: Historical turbulence as the round 4 lean - roll for a world with fewer or more countries
items.design:
RETURNED TO THE POOL 2026-09-09, unbuilt and unchanged. This was planned for sprint 36 and never started. Ben redirected that sprint mid-flight: the rules for initial colonisation and the peaceful spreading of societies are vastly different from those of war and empire, and this item is EMPIRE-PHASE - it only bites once there is something to fight over. Applying it to a span that is overwhelmingly settlement (839 foundings against 9 battles on seed 0, measured) is what would force the fixture-fitting the redirect exists to avoid. Re-scope it against whatever phase boundary sprint 37 settles on before building it.

BEN, 2026-09-08: "we are really looking to encourage historical turbulence as a parameter - so that players can roll for worlds which have fewer countries at this step, or more countries at this step".

THIS SUPERSEDES BL-818's PLACEHOLDER AXES. That item said the axes were the design work and were not settled; this is the settlement, and it is a better axis than any of the four guessed at, because the player can WATCH it resolve on the very map round 4 is showing them. A lean whose effect is invisible on its own round is not worth offering.

IT TUNES FORCES AND NEVER CLAMPS A COUNT. A turbulence lean moves the SPREAD of culture aggression, how sharply neighbours coalesce against a riser (BL-838), and how fast reach decays with distance (BL-837). It does not target a number of nations, and it must not acquire a post-hoc correction that does. The 2026-07-30 emergent-nation-count ruling, BL-224's non-hegemony invariant and GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § Asymmetry is the deliverable all survive intact: fragmented or consolidated is an OUTCOME, not a quota.

CULTURE AGGRESSION IS WHERE THE TUNING LANDS. polity::aggression_q already exists, derived from the culture's own aggression_q (BL-277 Q5). Two archetypes are worth having and they are not the same shape: one that EXPANDS AND INCORPORATES, absorbing the conquered and growing large and durable; one that CYCLES - unifying, stabilising, fragmenting and re-unifying on a rhythm. The same engine produces different turbulence signatures from them, which is why a SPREAD of aggression profiles is worth more than a single dial.

THE STANDING RULE APPLIES AND IS NOT SOFTENED. Both archetypes are drawn from real history as MECHANISMS, exactly as HISTORY.md's institutional ladder is. What transfers is the mechanism; a proper noun never does. No generated name in Io is Earth-derived, and this item must not become a name bank - see GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § Real history in, invented names out.

DONE WHEN: the lean moves the epoch nation-count DISTRIBUTION across a seed sweep in the expected direction, at both settings, with no term targeting a count; and a world at either setting is still a legitimate world.

items.author: BL-835 verification (2026-09-09); Ben's call to file it separately; Claude
items.title: In the quiet worlds every battle is still a conquest, and nothing yet says why
items.design:
FILED ON BEN'S CALL when BL-835 was closed (2026-09-09): the pathology BL-835 was written against is gone, and what is left is a smaller and different question that deserves its own item rather than holding that one open.

WHAT WAS FIXED. BL-835 removed the cause of the dead-region ping-pong. The seed-0 fixture went from 258 battles on ONE zero-population region - battles == conquests == 258, exactly 1:1 - to 9 battles across a world that grows from 533 to 1,372 regions. The signature is gone.

WHAT REMAINS. Several seeds still show battles == conquests exactly. Measured on the merged tree: seed 0 at 9 battles / 8 conquests, and the world_determinism fixtures at 4/4 (seed A) and 65/49 (seed B), 30/13 (the 1960 arc). The worlds that DO fight at volume have broken the 1:1 ratio; the quiet worlds have not. At 4 to 9 battles across four thousand years the ratio may be nothing but small numbers - nine coin flips landing the same way is not evidence of a weighted coin - or it may be that in a world with almost no armies, any attack that is worth launching at all is one that cannot be resisted.

THE ITEM IS TO FIND OUT WHICH, AND IT IS A MEASUREMENT BEFORE IT IS A FIX. Do not tune anything against the ratio until a seed sweep says whether it survives at volume. The instrument exists: history_sim_harness already prints battles and conquests unaided, and B384a ('every world sees at least one region change hands by war') and B384c currently FAIL because several seeds fight zero times - which is itself part of the same question.

RELATED AND POSSIBLY THE REAL ANSWER: Ben's 2026-09-09 observation that the rules for initial colonisation and the peaceful spreading of societies are vastly different from those of war and empire, and that stage 4 may want to be two phases rather than one. A span that is overwhelmingly settlement - 839 foundings against 9 battles on seed 0 - being scored by empire-phase rules is a candidate explanation for every symptom in this item. See the sprint 37 goal.

DONE WHEN: a seed sweep says whether battles == conquests survives at volume, and either a cause is named or the ratio is recorded as small-number noise and the item closed.

MEASURED 2026-09-10, 16 seeds on current main. The item asked whether battles == conquests survives at volume. ANSWER: IT IS NOT UNIVERSAL, and both the "small-number noise" hypothesis and a naive "it survives" reading are too simple.

  seed 2   141 battles / 141 conquests   exactly 1:1 at volume
  seed 3    53 / 53                      exactly 1:1
  seed 8    61 / 61                      exactly 1:1
  seed 9    79 / 79                      exactly 1:1
  seed 4   117 / 23                      breaks hard
  seed 7   137 / 35                      breaks hard
  seed 12   89 / 30                      breaks hard

So some worlds are exactly 1:1 at over a hundred battles -- far past coin-flip territory -- while others resolve four battles for every conquest. The ratio is a property of the WORLD, not of small numbers. What distinguishes the two groups is the question, and it is a real one: in a 1:1 world every attack that is launched is one that cannot be resisted, which says something about how defence is scored.

RELATED: BL-889 was re-measured the same session and reframed -- conquest is far too RARE (25 regions per world) rather than too consequence-free. These two items are looking at the same scoring behaviour from different sides and should be settled together.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-09, the Empires design pass); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Some peoples grow armies and begin to conquer, and which ones is downstream of their route
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-09: depending on their creed, some cultures grow armies and begin to conquer.

THE INPUT ALREADY EXISTS AND IS ALREADY EARNED. culture::aggression_q derives from the pantheon's war god, and COLONISATION.md sec Culture arrives by route made the distribution of pantheons a RECORD OF ROUTES. So which peoples turn warlike is downstream of where their ancestors walked -- which is exactly the ordering the colonisation design set out to establish: doctrine is downstream of how a people came to live where it lives.

NOT EVERY PEOPLE CONQUERS, AND THAT IS THE POINT. A world where every culture musters is as flat as one where none does.

NOT A NEW AI GRANT. A polity choosing to campaign is a decision, and this phase HAS actors where the migration span deliberately has none -- but it is the Era -1 sim's EXISTING scored-utility verb set, already covered by the dated register in AI_OPPONENT.md sec 11, bound by the same constraints: pure, seeded, deterministic, replayable, only legal verbs, never a planner. ANYTHING BEYOND THOSE FIVE VERBS IS A NEW WIDENING AND IS BEN'S TO GIVE -- raised, never assumed.

DONE WHEN: the spread of who conquers correlates with route-derived aggression across a seed sweep, and a warlike people and a peaceable one are both normal outcomes.
items.resolution:
DIAGNOSIS SUPERSEDED 2026-09-10 (this session). The seven failed verification attempts were not seven bad fixtures; they were one correct signal, misread each time.

WHAT THE PRIOR NOTE SAID: two_polity_world stopped producing conquests once BL-837 (reach gate) and BL-872 (supply floor) landed, so the fixture needed rebuilding for the post-BL-837/872 world.

WHAT THE SWEEP ACTUALLY SHOWS. history_sweep at 16 seeds on main: 386 conquests in the median world, 0 polities eliminated in 16 of 16 worlds, largest empire 3.3%, rise/peak/fall in 0/16 worlds. Conquest is not suppressed -- it is CONSTANT and CONSEQUENCE-FREE, everywhere, not just in this item's fixture. BL-889 (conquest must compound) owns that finding.

WHY THAT MAKES THIS ITEM UNTESTABLE AS WRITTEN. w_aggr_q leans WHICH polity chooses to campaign. In a world where campaigning already happens 386 times and compounds into nothing, a lean on that choice produces no measurable difference in outcome -- there is no outcome for it to differ in. Every clean test design would still read as noise. That is why passes 1-7 could not find a signal: the signal is not there to find yet.

THE WIRING IS STILL SOUND AND IS STILL WORTH KEEPING. w_aggr_q as a proportional lean symmetric around neutral 500, same idiom as w_cult/w_dist, plus pass 6's test design (hold the DEFENDER at neutral aggression, measure time-to-first-conquest across a seed sweep). It sits rebased and unmerged in .claude/worktrees/agent-aec88315766979641 (commit b6d04c6c / ea2b1111 on ed229efb).

NOW BLOCKED ON BL-889. Once conquest compounds, this item gets a route it never had: a warlike creed should produce a LARGER or FASTER empire, which is a difference the sweep can see. Verify it distributionally on history_sweep rather than on a two-polity fixture -- and per Ben (2026-09-10) a seed that refuses war is a legitimate outcome, so the claim is about the spread, never about every world.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-10, watching Round 4 live); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Reach propagates through chains of population centres, not one capital radius
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-10, watching BL-837 (ancient logistics and roads) play out live in Round 4: "Reach should be propagated by chains of population centres. This is a logistics question no? We can treat logistic points as a side effect of larger population centres too."

THE PROBLEM BL-837 SHOWED, live rather than on paper. Reach gating one Dijkstra from a single capital works as designed -- BL837a/b/c all pass, the mechanism is sound -- but it produces too few small polities surviving the round, and B384c (a death spiral must terminate somewhere in a sweep) fails: a shrinking polity's last holdout can end up permanently beyond its own contracting single-capital radius, in a way pure pricing never allowed. Floor recalibration (250 -> 80 -> 20) does not move this -- it is structural, not a tuning problem (see BL-837's resolution note and CIVILISATION.md sec Open questions).

THE PROPOSED FIX IS ARCHITECTURAL. Reach should propagate through a NETWORK of population centres -- hopping seat to seat, or centre to centre, along roads -- rather than radiating from one capital by Dijkstra. Ben's own framing ties this to the existing Logistic Points concept (../economy/LOGISTICS.md): larger population centres would generate Logistic Points as a side effect, and those points (or the network they imply) are what carries reach onward, rather than a single distance-from-capital number.

WHY THIS ALSO MATTERS BEYOND B384c. Ben's stated goal is a "new world" for a later exploration/colonisation phase to still find -- meaning round 4 should not fully partition every last scrap of the map into a handful of surviving empires. A chain-based reach model, where a network can genuinely fail to extend into some ground, is one candidate mechanism for leaving real unclaimed territory behind, distinct from B384c's narrower death-spiral question but plausibly solved by the same rework.

TIES DIRECTLY TO BL-872 (centres from supply/governance, not yet built) -- that item already asks what a population centre IS in this phase (derived by supply and governance), and this item asks what a centre DOES for reach. They may turn out to be the same piece of work, or BL-872 may need to land first to give this item real centres to chain through.

DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT NOW. Ben: wants tech progression wired into these generation rounds first, so this is a later-sprint item, not an immediate follow-up to BL-837. B384c stays a known, accepted failure in the interim (see BL-837's resolution).

DONE WHEN: reach is computed as propagation through a chain/network of population centres rather than a single capital-Dijkstra; B384c's death-spiral invariant holds again across a seed sweep; and round 4 measurably leaves some ground unclaimed rather than fully partitioning the map, in a way a later exploration phase could plausibly build on.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-10); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Campaign loses the verb contest 99 times in 100, so the world settles instead of fighting
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-10, on being shown the sweep: "Really I want to see polities be eliminated and empires to form, before collapsing back into those smaller polities - with some surviving as larger kingdoms."

MEASURED, NOT REASONED. history_sweep, 16 seeds, main at c83a0d74 (this session):
  battles per world      median 412   range 4..1000
  conquests per world    median 386   range 4..740
  worlds with 0 conquest 0 / 16
  LARGEST polity share   median 3.3%  range 2.1%..5.4%
  polities ELIMINATED    0, in 16 of 16 worlds (powers_start == powers_end everywhere)
  rise/peak/fall shape   0 / 16 worlds
  hegemony               never (hegemony_year == -1 x16)
With 31-61 powers per world an EVEN split is 1.6-3.2%. The biggest empire anywhere reaches 3.3%.

THE DEFECT IS NOT VOLUME, IT IS COMPOUNDING. 386 conquests per world and the political map ends the shape it started. Each transfer leaves the winner no better placed to win the next, so success never runs away with itself. All four of Ben's moments -- elimination, empire, collapse, uneven survival -- are consequences of that single property, not four dials.

THIS SUPERSEDES THE BL-868 DIAGNOSIS. NEXT_SESSION.md and BL-868's own resolution blamed a broken two_polity_world fixture for seven failed verification attempts. The fixture was reporting the truth: conquest is capped everywhere, not just there. An aggression lean cannot be measured as a difference in who conquers while conquest changes nothing for anybody.

THE LEADING SUSPECT IS THE REACH GATE, AND IT IS EVIDENCED, NOT ASSUMED. history_sim_harness on main fails R3a2 and R3a3 with the trace "near: 6 battles / 1 conquests | far: 0 battles / 0 conquests" -- and that case DELIBERATELY sets neighbour_radius=40 and w_dist=0 so that ONLY supply decay can stop the far target. Zero campaigns reach it. Something vetoes distance outright before supply is ever priced, and sustainable_campaign_floor_q is the hard gate BL-837 added. Its own comment already records the prior investigation: floors of 80 and 20 -- two orders of magnitude apart -- produced IDENTICAL elimination counts, which rules out a calibration fix, and names the mechanism ("a hard gate removes that long tail entirely").

THE TENSION IS REAL AND IS BEN'S TO RESOLVE. Ben ruled 2026-09-09 that reach GATES a campaign rather than pricing it, precisely so a rich polity cannot buy past geography. That ruling and this one pull against each other: a wall stops compounding by construction. CIVILISATION.md sec The arc the phase must produce states the tension rather than resolving it, and history_sim.hpp already carries "80 IS WHERE THIS SHIPS, PENDING BEN'S CALL".

DONE WHEN: across a history_sweep spread, worlds show the arc -- polities eliminated, a polity reaching a share materially above an even split, that polity then falling, and surviving fragments of visibly unequal size. Distributional, never per-world: a peaceable seed is a legitimate outcome (Ben, 2026-09-10) and must not be forced. NO TARGET NUMBER IS SET HERE -- the threshold comes off the measured spread, not ahead of it.

RULED 2026-09-10 (Ben, on NR-823): THE WALL MOVES WHEN YOU WIN. The 2026-09-09 reach-GATES-not-prices ruling stands -- geography cannot be bought past. What resolves the tension with this item is that the gate is NOT FIXED: reach is a function of the road network a polity has built and walked, so winning extends the wall outward. Geography must be BUILT past, and building past it is what an empire is.

REJECTED, so they are not re-litigated. Softening the gate into a steep price (would reverse the 2026-09-09 ruling and let a rich polity buy past geography). Centre-chain propagation (BL-887) -- the eventual reach model, deliberately still deferred until tech progression is wired into these rounds.

WHAT THAT MAKES LOAD-BEARING. This item may NOT be delivered by lowering sustainable_campaign_floor_q -- that is the softening Ben declined, and it is separately ruled out by measurement (floors of 80 and 20 give identical elimination counts). The work is in the mechanism by which success WIDENS reach. BL-892 records that mechanism failing today: W7b shows a pre-built reach work does not change the supply path at all. A wall that cannot move IS the fixed wall this ruling declines, so BL-892 is a prerequisite in substance even where it is not one in code.

=== REFRAMED 2026-09-10 ON RE-MEASUREMENT. THE NUMBERS ABOVE ARE STALE AND THE DIAGNOSIS THEY CARRY IS WRONG. ===

The figures this item was filed on (412 battles / 386 conquests per world) were measured at c83a0d74, BEFORE sprint 37 landed. Sprint 37 -- settlement-locked provinces (BL-849), contact-derived fragmentation (BL-852), rivers in the sim view (BL-853), the neighbour-degree cap (BL-855), wider habitability (BL-888) -- changed the world the sim runs on. Re-measured on current main, 16 seeds:

  battles per world      median 61   (was 412)   range 7..141
  conquests per world    median 35   (was 386)
  foundings per world    median 2682
  largest polity share   median 2.8%              range 2.0%..4.5%
  polities ELIMINATED    0, in 16 of 16 worlds
  hegemony               never

CONFLICT FELL ROUGHLY TEN-FOLD ACROSS SPRINT 37 AND NOBODY MEASURED IT. That is a finding in its own right. BL-855's max_neighbour_degree = 10 is the obvious suspect -- fewer neighbours means fewer campaign candidates -- but it is a suspect, not a conclusion.

THE CHURN HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED. A per-region transfer histogram (added this session, foundings excluded) reads: 25 regions ever conquered per world, 90% of them taken ONCE AND KEPT, 0% taken three or more times, 1.12 changes per conquered region. Conquest ACCUMULATES perfectly well. There is simply almost none of it -- 25 regions across ~40 polities and ~2,700 foundings, well under one region per polity across an entire history.

SO THE DEFECT IS NOT "conquest is frictionless and consequence-free". It is: A CAMPAIGN ALMOST NEVER HAPPENS. An empire cannot form out of 25 transfers however well each one sticks.

THE LARGEST NAMED SUPPRESSOR IS TRAVERSAL LEGALITY, NOT THE REACH GATE. The same sweep reports 812,424 campaigns REFUSED on traversal legality across 16 worlds -- about 50,000 per world against 61 battles actually fought. That is BL-778's water gate: a land force may not cross sea it does not own, and the sim's adjacency is a water-blind Chebyshev radius. The reach gate (R3a2/R3a3, still failing) is a second suppressor and its denials are not separately counted by the sweep.

WHAT THIS ITEM NOW OWES, in order: (1) count the refusal reasons separately in history_sweep -- traversal legality vs reach gate vs score threshold -- because 50,000 refusals per world with one named reason is not a diagnosis; (2) establish whether the water gate is refusing campaigns between polities that a player would consider neighbours; (3) only then decide what changes. Do NOT tune sustainable_campaign_floor_q -- Ben declined that softening (NR-823) and it is separately ruled out by measurement.

THE NR-823 RULING STILL HOLDS AND IS NOW MORE POINTED. "The wall moves when you win" needs a polity to win something first. At 25 transfers per world it essentially never gets to.

=== DIAGNOSED 2026-09-10. THREE HYPOTHESES TESTED AND KILLED; THE FOURTH IS MEASURED. ===

Traced 16-seed sweep on current main, median per world:
  contacts examined      2,109,795
    REFUSED traversal       42,366   = 2% of contacts (BL-778 water gate)
    REFUSED reach gate           0   (BL-837)
  ROUND grain:
  Campaign in the running  5,204 rounds
    ...WON the argmax           61   = 1.2%
    ...LOST the argmax       5,115   = 98.8%
  foundings                2,682     conquests 35

KILLED: (1) THE CHURN HYPOTHESIS -- 90% of conquered regions are taken once and KEPT, 0% taken 3+ times. Conquest compounds fine. (2) THE REACH GATE -- denies literally nothing in a generated world; it bites only in the synthetic R3a2 fixture where the target sits 34 tiles out. Every prior diagnosis of this item named it, including this session's own first hypothesis. (3) THE WATER GATE -- 2% of contacts, not a suppressor.

THE CAUSE: VERB COMPETITION. Campaign is a live candidate in 5,204 decision rounds per world and wins 61. Nothing blocks war; the scorer prefers something else 99 times in 100, and what it prefers is Settle -- 2,682 foundings against 35 conquests. A world with empty ground to take peacefully has no reason to take ground violently.

SO THIS IS A SCORING-PRIORITY QUESTION, NOT A MECHANISM ONE, and the item's original framing (reach, supply, compounding) is wrong throughout.

THE CONSTRAINT ON THE FIX IS THE STANDING RULE, and it bites hard here. A lever must be a FORCE WITH A VISIBLE CAUSE ON THE MAP, never a term inside an actor. Raising w_campaign, or lowering campaign_threshold_q, is precisely a thumb on the actor's own weights -- the shape the rule forbids, and the shape Ben declined for the reach gate in NR-823.

THE ADMISSIBLE SHAPE, for Ben's call: make SETTLING stop being the easy answer, rather than making war artificially attractive. A frontier that fills up -- once there is no cheap unclaimed ground within reach, Settle stops winning the argmax on its own merits and Campaign starts clearing on its own merits. That is an in-world force with a visible cause (the map runs out of room) and needs no term inside the scorer. It also matches Ben's arc: empires form when expansion stops being free.

MEASURED SUPPORT FOR THAT READING: 2,682 foundings per world against ~2,700 regions ever founded means settlement is still running at the end of the span. The frontier never closes, so the peaceful option never expires.

ALSO ESTABLISHED THIS SESSION: sprint 37 cut conflict roughly ten-fold (battles 412 -> 61, conquests 386 -> 35) and nothing measured it at the time. BL-855's max_neighbour_degree = 10 is the obvious suspect. Whether that is a regression or the correct new baseline is Ben's call and is NOT settled here.

NEXT STEP IS A DESIGN CALL, NOT A COMMIT. Do not tune a weight to close this item.

=== THE FIX IS BL-894, AND IT IS BEN'S, NOT A WEIGHT (2026-09-11) ===

Ben, 2026-09-11: "For our stage, land should already be settled. Settle in our stage is just a consequence of when polities decide to raze settlements and destroy cultures."

That closes the question this item's diagnosis left open. Campaign does not lose the argmax because it is under-weighted; it loses because SETTLE IS ALWAYS AVAILABLE. history_sim.cpp sec Settle fires on population pressure and manufactures new ground indefinitely -- a migration-era verb running inside an empire-era round. Re-scope it to RE-settlement of razed ground (BL-894) and peaceful expansion stops being free, at which point Campaign clears on its own merits.

This item is now blocked on BL-894 and becomes its ACCEPTANCE MEASUREMENT: does the arc appear once the frontier closes.

CAVEAT ON EVERY NUMBER IN THIS ITEM: they were measured WITHOUT --epoch, i.e. on history_sim_params struct defaults (4000 BCE -> 0 CE, six bands), which is NOT what generation runs (-400 -> 0 on one four-year band). That is the BL-462 divergence the harness header warns about, and it means the founding counts quoted here INCLUDE the migration era. Re-measure on --epoch before treating any of them as a property of the Empires round.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-10); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: The wizard opens on seed 0, so every new game is the same reference world unless you press Roll
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-10: "Let's lose the framing of seeded worlds, and make world generation entirely random. This comes at the cost of having newer data to examine each test, but it allows the player to have a higher degree of chance when they do choose to reroll, and it gives the player the ability to see if their world will contain these types of structures."

SCOPE, SETTLED BY BEN THE SAME DAY (elicitation, "wizard-default-only"). The wizard's OPENING seed is rolled. Harnesses, goldens and the sweep keep passing seeds explicitly and are untouched.

WHAT IS ALREADY THERE. startup_screens.cpp:333 already has hex entry, a Roll button drawing from std::random_device, and Copy seed, with the comment "no entropy ever enters world generation, which stays a pure function of this seed". The gap is only that world_params::seed defaults to 0 -- hard_coded_world.hpp:41, "0 reproduces the legacy world" -- and nothing rolls it on entry, so m_pending_world_params is default-constructed and the player must know to press Roll.

NOT A DETERMINISM WIDENING, AND THIS IS THE POINT. The entropy stops at the UI exactly as the existing Roll button's does. world/* stays a pure function of the seed, so save, replay and the multiplayer argument are untouched and no standing-rule grant is needed. Seed 0 still names the reference world; it is simply no longer what a player gets by accident.

DONE WHEN: arriving at New World shows a freshly rolled seed, the player can still type or paste one, and a run at a given seed is identical to before.
items.resolution:
DELIVERED 2026-09-10 (2334ac11, corrected in e8fe7d82). LIVE-CHECKED against build/ProjectIo.exe.

THE LIVE CHECK CAUGHT A REGRESSION, which is exactly what the standing rule exists for and a clean compile would have shipped. The first cut rolled in open_new_world_wizard. That function runs when the player presses New Game -- ON THE WAY OUT of the menu that carries the seed field -- so it silently discarded any seed just typed or pasted, breaking hex entry and Copy seed. The menu also still showed 00000000, so the item's visible purpose was unmet too.

CORRECT SEAM: the menu draw, behind a one-shot latch (app::m_seed_rolled). Idempotent -- fresh on arrival, then the player's. Rolling per frame would make the field impossible to type into.

LIVE EVIDENCE: menu opens on 705D7EAE; relaunch gives 25932312 (different world); typing 1234ABCD sticks; Roll then gives 98D91A1B. Suppressed under --verify (m_golden_dir non-empty), so the visual suite stays deterministic.

DETERMINISM UNTOUCHED: entropy stops at the UI exactly as the Roll button's does; world/* stays a pure function of the seed. Seed 0 still names the reference world.

GRANTED-PATH TRAP HIT AGAIN while verifying: computer-use resolved "ProjectIo" to a STALE worktree build (.claude/worktrees/elated-mclean-7dd61c, dated Sep 9, predating this item). Launch the main-checkout exe explicitly and grant the basename projectio.exe. The window also opened on LS24DG30X, not the BenQ -- the request_access response reports the display and is more reliable than any note.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-10); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: A rolled world cannot be judged, because round 4 never shows whether the arc happened in it
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-10, the second half of the randomise ruling: rolling should give "the player the ability to see if their world will contain these types of structures". Ben placed this IN sprint 38 (elicitation, "in-sprint-38").

RANDOMNESS WITHOUT A READOUT IS NOT A CHOICE. BL-890 makes each arrival a fresh world; this item is what lets the player tell one from another. Without it a reroll is a blind redraw -- the player cannot see whether this world produced an empire, a collapse, or five polities that never fought, so "reroll until it looks interesting" is not actually available to them.

THE STRUCTURES ARE THE ONES GENERATION_STRATEGY.md sec The asymmetry is POLITICAL names: were polities eliminated, did an empire form, did it fall, are the survivors unequal. history_sweep already computes every one of these per world (eliminations, top/peak share, BL-767 rise/peak/fall) -- the quantities exist and are simply not surfaced.

RELATED SURFACES ALREADY DESIGNED: BL-817 (history playback record) and BL-830 (top-sixteen scoreboard) are round 4's instrument. Check what they now cover before adding a surface -- this may be a read on those rather than a new panel. SCOPE THAT FIRST.

DONE WHEN: after round 4 the player can see, without leaving the wizard, whether this world's history contains the arc -- and can reroll on that basis.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-10); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: W7b fails: pre-built reach works do not change the supply path, so reach_mod reads as inert
items.design:
FOUND BY RUNNING history_sweep ON MAIN, 2026-09-10 (this session), at c83a0d74. The sweep's only red:

  FAIL  W7b  pre-built reach changes the supply path -- reach_mod is read, not inert

with the trace immediately above it reading "reach seeded: 1 battles / 0 stalled | plain: 1 / 0" -- identical with and without seeded reach works, which is exactly what the check is written to catch.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A LONE RED. w_work_reach exists so a polity can BUILD its way to further reach, and CIVILISATION.md sec The road is the empire's skeleton makes reach the thing that gates conquest. If a reach work does not move the supply path, then the one lever a polity has for extending its own reach does nothing -- which bears directly on BL-889 (conquest must compound), where inability to extend reach is the leading explanation for why no empire ever forms. Diagnose the two together.

FOLDED INTO SPRINT 38 ON BEN'S CALL (2026-09-10, elicitation, "fold-into-38") rather than filed as its own stream.

DONE WHEN: W7b passes because a seeded reach work demonstrably changes the supply path, or the check is retired with a stated reason if the mechanism it asserts was superseded.

RAISED TO PRIORITY A, 2026-09-10, by Ben's NR-823 ruling. The ruling makes the arc depend on reach WIDENING as a polity succeeds -- "the wall moves when you win". This item is the record of that widening mechanism being inert. It is no longer a lone harness red; it is the lever BL-889 (conquest must compound) rests on.
items.resolution:
DELIVERED 2026-09-10 (d250dee6). THE FILED PREMISE WAS WRONG AND THAT IS THE HEADLINE: reach_mod was never inert.

MEASURED on W7b's own rival_strip(5, 800, 600, 500) fixture, by an instrument added for the purpose: work_reach_mod sums to 3200 across the ten seeded regions (120 Test Way + 200 Test Mole each) and network_supply_q sums to 22038 seeded against 21680 plain -- a delta of 358, about 3.6% of supply per region. Applied, read, and arithmetically exactly as authored.

THE DEFECT WAS THE ALTITUDE OF THE ASSERTION. W7b asserted on OUTCOMES (battles, conquests, foundings, owner_changes). reach_mod discounts the terrain term of supply, and supply is one input among several to a threshold decision -- 3.6% cannot flip a campaign choice on a ten-region strip. So the check could not tell "working as authored" from "disconnected entirely", and the backlog recorded the null result as the mechanism being dead.

A SECOND SUPPLY PATH WAS FOUND WHILE PROVING THE FIX, and it is the more useful finding for BL-889. Capping the discount off drops the delta from 358 to 16 but NOT to zero: reach_mod reaches supply TWICE OVER -- once through the terrain discount (342 of the delta) and once through the reach Dijkstra itself, which a cheaper network also shortens (16). The two paths differ in strength by roughly 20:1. A plain "seeded > plain" assertion therefore still passes with the discount fully dead, which would have rebuilt the old check's weakness one level down.

THE CHECK IS NOW DIFFERENTIAL: the seeded-vs-plain supply delta with the discount live must exceed twice the delta with work_reach_relief_cap_q forced to 0. No absolute threshold, so there is nothing to tune toward. W7b1 was added alongside it so a vacuous fixture (no works applied) fails loudly rather than passing quietly.

DISCONNECTION PROOF, run both directions. Zeroing the discount at both read sites in history_sim.cpp: "discount live: +16 | discount capped off: +16", W7b RED. Restored: "+358 | +16", W7b PASS. history_sim.cpp was left unchanged.

CONSEQUENCE FOR BL-889 AND FOR NR-823. Ben's ruling is that the wall moves when you win. There are two mechanisms by which it moves and they are ~20:1 in strength. If reach-widening proves too weak to let empires form, that ratio is the first place to look; nothing measured it before this item.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-10); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: A force can take coastal ground from across the water when the land behind it outweighs the defender
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-10: "units can move into and capture coast tiles if the adjoined land province has a higher population count than the defender".

THE RULE. Today the water gate (BL-778, history_sim.cpp sec THE WATER GATE) refuses a campaign outright when the contact is not dry, the attacker owns no shore at the target, and its military band cannot field naval. It is a hard legality test with no way past it. This item adds ONE way past it, and makes it a question about WEIGHT rather than about ships: a coastal target may be taken from across the water when the attacker's adjoining land province carries more population than the defender.

WHY IT IS ADMISSIBLE UNDER THE STANDING RULE. A lever must be a FORCE WITH A VISIBLE CAUSE ON THE MAP, never a term inside an actor and never a penalty scaling with a polity's rank. Population in an adjacent province is exactly that: it is on the map, the player can see it, and it is symmetric -- the same rule lets a heavy neighbour take from you. It reads as the obvious thing (a populous shore can force a narrow crossing) rather than as a dial.

=== IT WILL NOT FIX BL-889, AND THE MEASUREMENT IS RECORDED HERE SO NOBODY LATER ASSUMES IT WILL ===

The premise this was raised on -- that the coast/water gate is what suppresses conquest -- was MEASURED FALSE the same day, on the traced 16-seed sweep:
  contacts examined      median 2,109,795 per world
    REFUSED traversal      median    42,366   = 2% of contacts (BL-778 water gate)
    REFUSED reach gate     median         0   (BL-837 -- denies nothing in a generated world)
  cleared the threshold  median   794,915  (candidate grain)
  Campaign won the verb  median        61  rounds
The water gate accounts for 2% of refusals. Campaign clears its own threshold constantly and then LOSES THE VERB CONTEST -- the world settles (median 2,682 foundings) instead of fighting. BL-889 owns that.

SO THIS ITEM IS WORTH BUILDING ON ITS OWN MERITS -- it removes an absolute wall and replaces it with a legible condition, which is better design regardless -- but it should be expected to move conquest counts by roughly the size of that 2%, not to produce empires.

OPEN QUESTIONS THE BUILD MUST SETTLE. (1) WHICH population -- the attacking region's own, or the whole adjoining province? Ben's words say province; region is what the sim indexes. (2) Does the crossing still cost supply, or is it free once the weight test passes? A free crossing would make coastal ground cheaper to take than inland ground, which inverts the intent. (3) Does it apply at every military band, or only once some rung is reached? The current gate already exempts polities that can_field_naval, so this must not make ships pointless. (4) Is the comparison strict (>) or does a tie fail? Strict, on the same reasoning ties fail elsewhere.

DONE WHEN: a coastal target with a heavier land province behind the attacker is takeable across water, the reverse case is still refused, illegal_campaigns falls by a measurable amount on the sweep, and ships are still worth having.

=== REFINED 2026-09-10 (Ben) ===

Q1 SETTLED: PROVINCES, not regions. The comparison is the adjoining land PROVINCE's population against the defender's. The sim indexes regions, so the build owes a province-level population rollup at the contact -- PROVINCES.md owns the spatial unit.

NAVAL ALREADY EXISTS, AND THAT SHARPENS Q3 RATHER THAN ANSWERING IT. Measured on the sweep: 5% of battles are reached over a sea leg, and MILITARY_HISTORY.md sec Naval states that rarity is the DESIGN. can_field_naval gates three roster rows on port_q, and the water gate ALREADY exempts any polity clearing it -- so ships are already the way past this wall.

THE RISK THIS CREATES, stated plainly: if a heavy province can cross without ships, then the port_q route matters only to LIGHT polities, which inverts who needs a navy. A big coastal power would stop building ships and just walk across on weight. Guarding that is part of the item, not an afterthought -- candidate answers are that the weight crossing costs supply a naval crossing does not, or that it is capped to a single province depth, or that it only applies where no naval option exists at that band.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Settle in the Empires round manufactures new ground forever, so peaceful growth always beats war
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-11: "For our stage, land should already be settled. Settle in our stage is just a consequence of when polities decide to raze settlements and destroy cultures."

THIS IS BL-889's FIX, and it is admissible where the obvious repair was not.

WHAT THE SCORER DOES TODAY. history_sim.cpp sec Settle fires on POPULATION PRESSURE against carrying capacity: a region nearing K spawns a daughter region. It never asks whether there is empty land -- it manufactures new ground. The comment states the purpose outright: "run_settlement founds every region before the stop year and leaves none after it, so without this verb a 2000-year run has a frozen region count." That is a MIGRATION-ERA justification running inside an EMPIRE-ERA round.

THE MEASURED CONSEQUENCE (traced 16-seed sweep, 2026-09-10, ROUND grain): Campaign is in the running 5,204 rounds per world and WINS 61 -- 1.2%. It loses the argmax 5,115 times. Nothing blocks war: the reach gate denies 0, the water gate accounts for 2% of contacts, and 90% of conquered ground is taken once and kept. Peaceful expansion is simply always available and always cheaper.

WHY A WEIGHT CHANGE IS NOT THE ANSWER. Raising w_campaign or lowering campaign_threshold_q is a term INSIDE THE ACTOR -- forbidden by the standing rule, and the same shape Ben declined for the reach gate on 2026-09-09 (NR-823). Re-scoping what Settle MEANS in this phase changes what is LEGAL, not what is preferred, and leaves the scorer honest.

THE RULE. In the Empires round, Settle is RE-settlement: the re-founding of ground that was emptied by a sack or a destroyed culture. It is downstream of violence and cannot fire on ground nobody has harmed. CIVILISATION.md sec Land is already settled when this phase opens carries the ruling.

OPEN QUESTIONS THE BUILD MUST SETTLE. (1) What marks ground as RESETTLEABLE -- a razed seat, a region whose population went to zero, a destroyed culture record? sack_region_urban and centres_razed already exist. (2) Does the migration span keep the old pressure-driven Settle? It must -- COLONISATION.md owns a diffusion that has to fill the map, and this rule is scoped to the Empires round only. The two spans therefore need DIFFERENT settle rules, which is a params question, not a code fork. (3) What stops the region count freezing, which is the stated reason the verb exists? Answer: nothing should -- a settled map with a fixed region count is the premise of this phase.

DONE WHEN: across a sweep of the GENERATION-DERIVED span (--epoch, not the struct defaults), foundings in the Empires round fall to roughly the razing rate, Campaign wins a materially larger share of the rounds it is in the running for, and the arc GENERATION_STRATEGY.md sec The asymmetry is POLITICAL asks for begins to appear. Distributional -- a peaceable seed stays legitimate.

MEASURE ON --epoch. The numbers above come from the struct-default 4000 BCE -> 0 CE span, which INCLUDES the migration era and therefore overstates how much settling belongs to this phase. The harness header calls that the BL-462 divergence. An --epoch run was started 2026-09-11 and its numbers belong in this item.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, the phase-outcome design session); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: A road joining unlike ground yields materials, so war is paid for by trade and not by nothing
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-11: "we also need a simple cost for war, and this cost can be sourced by rich trade."

THE COST HALF IS BUILT. BL-867 (materials spent on action) already charges a campaign in materials. What is missing is the INCOME -- today nothing funds it, so the cost is a drain with no counterpart and cannot discriminate between a rich polity and a poor one.

THE CONSTRAINT, AND IT IS NOT NEGOTIABLE. This phase has NO MARKET. CIVILISATION.md sec Materials are spent when something happens (Ben, 2026-09-09) is unchanged: no order book, no firm, no building stack, no price. Ben re-affirmed the exclusion on 2026-09-11 when offered the chance to reopen it, choosing "network income, no market".

SO THE INCOME IS A PROPERTY OF THE NETWORK. A road joining ground that holds DIFFERENT things yields materials; a road joining two places holding the same thing yields little. Only DIFFERENCE is read -- never a price for either side, and never a quantity that behaves like one. CIVILISATION.md sec War is paid for, and trade is what pays owns this.

IT DOES THREE JOBS AT ONCE, which is why it is worth its difficulty: (1) roads become worth building for a reason other than reach, so BL-837 stops being the only argument for a network; (2) war becomes affordable to the rich and unaffordable to the poor, producing asymmetry in campaigning WITHOUT a term inside any actor -- the standing rule's requirement; (3) network failure becomes expensive, giving the collapse ruling teeth: a realm whose roads fail loses its income before it loses its ground.

THE RESOURCE READING STAYS ABSTRACT. Resources become capital in pass 2 and that reading must not leak backwards (CIVILISATION.md sec What this phase hands the industrial era). What is needed here is only that two places hold unlike things.

DONE WHEN: a polity connected to unlike ground sustains campaigns a disconnected one cannot, the effect shows on history_sweep as a spread in campaign affordability, and no price, order book or firm has entered the phase.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, the phase-outcome design session); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: An empire fragments when it can no longer reach itself, and what it leaves is the next phase input
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-11 (ruling, from four candidates): collapse is NETWORK FAILURE. Succession, exhaustion and external shock were all offered and none was chosen.

THIS PROMOTES AN INCUMBENT READING TO A RULING. CIVILISATION.md sec What this phase hands the industrial era already said "reach-gating is what makes the collapse mechanical rather than scripted... never a collapse event fired at a date". That is now the settled cause rather than the likely one.

WHAT THE DARK AGE MUST LEAVE (Ben, same session; CIVILISATION.md sec What the dark age must leave):
  1. NATIONS OF UNEQUAL STRENGTH -- some able to colonise, some only to be colonised.
  2. ROADS THAT OUTLIVE THEIR BUILDERS -- the network survives the empire, inherited unevenly.
  3. GRUDGES THAT STILL BITE -- carried today, inert today (BL-898 owns making them consequential).

GROUND RELEASED BACK TO NOBODY WAS DECLINED, and the reason is load-bearing rather than a detail: a colonial era colonises INHABITED ground. What a coloniser wants is land held by someone weaker with people already on it, not empty land. Unequal nations ARE the new world, so nothing needs emptying for the next phase to have somewhere to go. This resolves the apparent tension with BL-887's note about leaving "a new world" for a later phase to find.

DONE WHEN: across a sweep, empires form and then fragment because their networks stop holding; the resulting nations differ materially in size; roads persist through the fragmentation; and no collapse fires on a date or a counter.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, the phase-outcome design session); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: A creed stops being one people's pantheon and becomes an answer for everyone
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-11: "We should use this phase to deepen religious understanding and turmoil... the prior work done on pantheons, being subsumed by [a universal faith], and providing a unity which spans through culture and language difference. This also provides another angle from which empires fall."

THE NAME IN BEN'S NOTE IS AN ANALOGY AND NEVER CONTENT. The standing rule is unconditional -- real history is a mechanism reference, never a name source. The universalising creed is generated and named by the same phoneme banks as every other creed. Nothing Earth-flavoured enters the game.

IT INVERTS THE ONE PROPERTY EVERY EXISTING CREED HAS. CREEDS.md sec The rule: one pantheon, one tongue makes a creed LOCAL BY CONSTRUCTION -- it belongs to a cradle culture and travels only as that people travels, which is what made pantheon distribution a record of routes. A universalising creed SUBSUMES the pantheons it meets rather than displacing their peoples, so it spreads along CONTACT rather than along ANCESTRY.

THREE JOBS NOTHING ELSE DOES. (1) UNITY ACROSS DIFFERENCE -- kinship and opposition are both computed from descent, so a shared creed is the first thing in the design that can bind two peoples who are not kin and share no tongue. That is what lets an empire hold ground its own culture never walked. (2) A MOTIVE TO EXPAND THAT IS NOT HUNGER FOR LAND -- a creed that believes it is for everyone supplies a reason to cross water toward PEOPLE rather than toward GROUND, which is what makes a colonial era look different from a border war. (3) A SECOND, INDEPENDENT WAY TO FALL -- BL-896 settles collapse as network failure; a schism, or a subsumed pantheon reasserting itself, fractures along lines that have nothing to do with distance. Two failure modes that fire separately is what stops the dark age having one shape.

THE TURMOIL IS THE POINT. A creed that only unified would flatten the world -- the same objection raised against RESOLVE as a civilisation formation rule (NR-817) and rejected there for the same reason. Subsumption must leave residue: the absorbed pantheon is still underneath, and it is what a schism is made of.

FOUR OPEN QUESTIONS THIS ITEM MUST SETTLE FIRST, and they are design rather than implementation: does a universalising creed arise from an existing pantheon or is it coined new; what makes one arise AT ALL rather than being scheduled (it must be a consequence of upstream scalars, never a roll or a date); may a people hold both its pantheon and the universal creed, or must it choose; and what does conversion of a POLITY mean as against conversion of a PEOPLE.

DONE WHEN: those four are settled and written into CREEDS.md, a universalising creed arises in some worlds and not others as a consequence of what came before, it binds unlike peoples measurably, and an empire somewhere in a sweep fractures over faith rather than over distance.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, the phase-outcome design session); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Grudges are carried across the handoff and then read by nothing
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-11, describing the phase he wants: cultures from the previous phase are carried forward WITH THEIR GRUDGES.

HALF OF THAT IS TRUE TODAY. CIVILISATION.md sec What the Culture phase must hand forward lists `pass_one_output::grudges` as CARRIED, and it is: the directed layer exists and records who wronged whom, at a place and a date, distinct from the symmetric opposition layer (NR-815). What is missing is any CONSUMER -- the grudge crosses the handoff and nothing reads it.

CARRIED IS NOT CONSEQUENTIAL, and the distinction is the one this project keeps relearning: a field that is retained but unread is indistinguishable from one never retained, except that it looks finished.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR THE PHASE OUTCOME. CIVILISATION.md sec What the dark age must leave names live grudges as one of three things the dark age must carry into a colonial era, on the reasoning that WHO COLONISES WHOM IS NOT A FRESH ROLL -- it is the last quarrel continued by other means. A grudge nothing reads cannot do that job.

THE CONSTRAINT. A grudge must act as a FORCE WITH A VISIBLE CAUSE, never a term inside an actor: it is a fact about a place and a date the player could in principle be shown, which is what makes it admissible where a bare aggression weight is not.

DONE WHEN: a grudge measurably changes who a polity campaigns against, two worlds differing only in their grudge record produce different targets, and the record stays legible as who-wronged-whom-where.
